Australian Metals & Mining Sector Posts Stable Growth Amid Strong Global Demand

Australia’s Metals & Mining sector delivered steady growth in the latest quarter, buoyed by resilient global demand and stable commodity prices. According to industry figures released on Thursday, total sector revenues climbed 4.2% year-on-year to AUD 52.8 billion, with iron ore and lithium exports leading the gains.

Chief Executive of MacPherson Resources, Ian McAllister, credited effective supply chain management and sustained international orders for the solid performance. “We’re seeing consistent buying from key Asian markets, particularly for battery minerals and premium iron ore,” McAllister said in a call with analysts.

Production volumes across major commodities were broadly unchanged from the previous quarter, reflecting a focus on operational discipline. The Australian Mining Council noted that total iron ore shipments reached 237 million tonnes for the first half of the year, while lithium concentrate output rose 9% to 312,000 tonnes.

“Stable market conditions and prudent cost controls have underpinned the sector’s resilience,” said analyst Priya Sharma of Goldside Securities. She added that ongoing infrastructure investment and a favorable regulatory environment continue to attract capital inflows.

Labour costs edged up 2.1% over the period amid ongoing skills shortages, though the Australian Workers’ Union said wage negotiations remained constructive, with no industrial action reported.

Looking ahead, the industry is expected to maintain its current trajectory, with analysts pointing to strong fundamentals and government support for minerals critical to energy transition technologies. Shares in leading miners closed modestly higher on Thursday, reflecting market confidence in the sector’s outlook.
